parsed.explanation: No traveller-facing exposure is documented: no presentation offence, no border or screening practice aimed at trans people, no bathroom/facility ban, and custody placement is expressly by gender identity — a documented positive. Gender identity and expression sit in the human-rights act and hate-crime provisions (2017), and one province's code has published policy and case law, giving a real (if untested for visitors) recourse route. Against that: six years of rising police-reported hate crime, an organised anti-trans movement, and provincial override statutes on schools/health/sport — but these are resident-facing or climate signals, and the 39% figure is LGBT-wide, not trans-specific prevalence. Other provinces' document procedures and anti-trans hate-crime levels are unresolved open questions, not documented exposures. Rule of law is intact and not turned against trans people, so this sits in the reduced-risk band, short of the acceptance-plus-demonstrated-enforcement anchors because no visitor remedy outcome is shown operating.
